research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10989 (27 FR 727, Federal Register of January 25, 1962), signed by John F. Kennedy and dated January 22, 1962; number, date and subject agree with the census register. Inventory: the dossier's three clauses (the lead-in, amendment 1 adding clauses (5) and (6) to section 2(a), and amendment 2 changing section 3 together with the effective-date sentence) are contiguous and cover every operative sentence; I confirm the inventory. The order further amends Executive Order 10168 of October 11, 1950, as amended (additional pay for sea and foreign duty of enlisted members): it adds two clauses treating duty on an artificial island such as a Texas Tower on the outer Continental Shelf as sea duty (clause (5) for assignment there, clause (6) for duty there of eight consecutive days or more while based ashore), amends section 3 to refer to clauses (3), (5) and (6), and makes the amendments effective as of the first day of the first month after the month of issue, that is 1962-02-01. Ending: Executive Order 11157 of June 22, 1964, section 502, revokes this order as item (k) and EO 10168 itself as item (c). The cited source is the held Federal Register text of EO 11157; the dossier's located-provision records for this pair that use a transcription mirror are not cited. Searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): the U.S. Code release point 119-121 and eCFR searches record no citation of this order; the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (two machine hits) are the revocation note on this order naming EO 11157 and the matching note on EO 11157 naming this order. EO 12553 does not list 10989 and no catalog note links them.

savings.reason: EO 11157 restates the artificial-island clauses in its own section 202(a)(5) and (6) ("While assigned to an artificial island (such as a Texas Tower)") and refers to them in section 203, so the substance continued under the new order; pay accrued under this order before 1964-06-22 is an accrued consequence. EO 11157 has no express savings clause in the held text, and no U.S. Code, eCFR or catalog hit shows any other continuing effect of this order.
